## What to look for

- Play from 1946: when do the colonial conflicts end?
- Which type of conflict is the most frequent in most years? Which type grows most after 2010?
- Find the peaks of the line of battle deaths since 1989. Which countries are red in those years?
- Compare a year of the Cold War, such as 1975, with the latest year: in which regions of the world are the conflicts located?

## How it works

The Uppsala Conflict Data Program (UCDP) counts a conflict in a year when the fighting between a government and another party (another government or an armed group) causes at least 25 battle-related deaths in that year; with 1 000 deaths or more, it is a war. The four types are colonial conflicts, conflicts between states, conflicts within a state, and conflicts within a state in which foreign troops fight on one side. The map colours the countries where UCDP locates the fighting, on today's borders; for a conflict between states, it colours the governments at war, even where no fighting took place on their own soil. Battle deaths (best estimates) are available from 1989 only.
